\chapter{Bigger, Better, For How Long}
\label{ch:ar-bigger-better-for-how-long}
\hlchaptermodality{290}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can compare two things, name the best, and say how long something has gone on or how long ago it happened.}

Complete AR-R290-comparing-and-time: compare with akbar min and afḍal, and measure with mundhu and qabla.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أكبر} \ar{من} (akbar min)}{أكبر من (akbar min)}]{\ar{أكبر} \ar{من} (akbar min) — bigger than}

\label{lesson:AR-C290-akbar-min}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}it was a new experience\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}I hope to travel\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Kānat tajribatan jadīda}, \emph{atamannā an usāfira}.)

To describe an experience well, you set it beside another: the city or the village, the train or the bus.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the shape aCCaC, and min}]
Take the three root letters of a describing word and pour them into the shape \emph{a-C-C-a-C}: \emph{kabīr}, big, becomes \textbf{\ar{أكبر}} \emph{akbar}, bigger; \emph{ṣaghīr} becomes \emph{aṣghar}; \emph{sarīʿ}, fast, becomes \emph{asraʿ}. \textbf{\ar{من}} — \emph{min}, \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{} — is the \textquotedblleft{}than\textquotedblright{}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{المدينة} \ar{أكبر} \ar{من} \ar{القرية}.} — \emph{al-madīna akbar min al-qarya} — The city is bigger than the village.
\end{quote}

The shape does not change for a feminine noun: \emph{al-madīna akbar}, \emph{al-qiṭār asraʿ min ad-darrāja}. You have owned two of these since chapter one hundred and seventy-six: \emph{akthar}, more, is the shape of \emph{kathīr}, many, and \emph{aqall}, less, of \emph{qalīl}, few.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the biggest, and better}]
Put \emph{al-} on it for \textquotedblleft{}the biggest\textquotedblright{}: \emph{al-akbar}. Or set it before a noun with no article: \textbf{\ar{أكبر} \ar{مدينة}} \emph{akbar madīna}, the biggest city.

\textquotedblleft{}Better\textquotedblright{} has a shape of its own: \textbf{\ar{أفضل}} \emph{afḍal}, from the root of \emph{faḍḍala}, to prefer, and of \emph{min faḍlik}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{القطار} \ar{أفضل} \ar{من} \ar{الحافلة}.} — \emph{al-qiṭār afḍal min al-ḥāfila} — The train is better than the bus.
\end{quote}

\emph{Al-afḍal} is \textquotedblleft{}the best\textquotedblright{}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kabīr} … \emph{akbar}; \emph{ṣaghīr} … \emph{aṣghar}; \emph{sarīʿ} … \emph{asraʿ}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The city is bigger than the village\textquotedblright{} — \emph{al-madīna akbar min al-qarya}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The train is faster than the bicycle\textquotedblright{} — \emph{al-qiṭār asraʿ min ad-darrāja}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}the biggest city\textquotedblright{} — \emph{akbar madīna}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I think the train is faster\textquotedblright{} — \emph{aʿtaqidu anna al-qiṭāra asraʿ}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The train is better than the bus\textquotedblright{} — \emph{al-qiṭār afḍal min al-ḥāfila}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}Bigger than\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Akbar min.}}) \textquotedblleft{}Smaller\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Aṣghar.}}) \textquotedblleft{}The best\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Al-afḍal.}}) Which two words were in this shape all along? (\emph{\textbf{Akthar}} and \emph{\textbf{aqall}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{منذ} \ar{ثلاث} \ar{سنوات} (mundhu thalāth sanawāt)}{منذ ثلاث سنوات (mundhu thalāth sanawāt)}]{\ar{منذ} \ar{ثلاث} \ar{سنوات} (mundhu thalāth sanawāt) — for three years}

\label{lesson:AR-C290-mundhu}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}the city is bigger than the village\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}the biggest city\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Al-madīna akbar min al-qarya}, \emph{akbar madīna}.)

An experience also has a length. \emph{Mundhu}, from chapter two hundred and thirty-three, measures it.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: mundhu and the present}]
For something that began in the past and is still going on, Arabic keeps the present and adds \emph{mundhu} with the span:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{أعمل} \ar{هنا} \ar{منذ} \ar{ثلاث} \ar{سنوات}.} — \emph{aʿmalu hunā mundhu thalāth sanawāt} — I have been working here for three years.
\end{quote}

English says \textquotedblleft{}have been working\textquotedblright{}; Arabic says \textquotedblleft{}I work, since three years\textquotedblright{}. With a point in time instead of a span, \emph{mundhu} is \textquotedblleft{}since\textquotedblright{}: \emph{anā hunā mundhu aṣ-ṣabāḥ}, I've been here since the morning.

Counting takes care. \emph{Sana}, a year, ends in \textbf{\ar{ة}}, and three to ten take the opposite ending to their noun: \emph{thalāth sanawāt}, three years, but \emph{thalāthat ashhur}, three months. For two, the noun takes \emph{-ayn}: \emph{sanatayn}, two years; \emph{usbūʿayn}, two weeks.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: ago}]
For a finished event, use the past and \textbf{\ar{قبل}} — \emph{qabla}, \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} — with the span:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{وصلت} \ar{قبل} \ar{أسبوع}.} — \emph{waṣaltu qabla usbūʿ} — I arrived a week ago.
\end{quote}

\emph{Mundhu} with a past verb can say \textquotedblleft{}ago\textquotedblright{} too: \emph{waṣaltu mundhu usbūʿ}. With the present it can only mean \textquotedblleft{}for\textquotedblright{}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have been working here for three years\textquotedblright{} — \emph{aʿmalu hunā mundhu thalāth sanawāt}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}for three months\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}for two weeks\textquotedblright{} — \emph{mundhu thalāthat ashhur}, \emph{mundhu usbūʿayn}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I arrived a week ago\textquotedblright{} — \emph{waṣaltu qabla usbūʿ}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have been learning Arabic for two years\textquotedblright{} — \emph{ataʿallamu al-ʿarabiyya mundhu sanatayn}
  \item how long you have lived where you live — \emph{askunu hunā mundhu …}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}For three years\textquotedblright{}, with a present? (\emph{\textbf{Mundhu thalāth sanawāt.}}) \textquotedblleft{}A week ago\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Qabla usbūʿ.}}) \textquotedblleft{}Two years\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Sanatayn.}}) Which tense goes with \emph{mundhu} for \textquotedblleft{}for\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{The present.})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — bigger, better, and for how long}

\label{lesson:AR-R290-comparing-and-time}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I was happy\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}I felt afraid\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Kuntu saʿīdan}, \emph{shaʿartu bi-l-khawf}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}I want to become an engineer\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Urīdu an uṣbiḥa muhandisan}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two lessons, and an experience can be weighed and measured. Weighed with the shape \emph{aCCaC} and \emph{min}: \emph{akbar min}, \emph{asraʿ min}, \emph{afḍal min}; with \emph{al-} or before a noun for the most: \emph{al-afḍal}, \emph{akbar madīna}. Measured with \emph{mundhu} and the present, for what is still going on, and \emph{qabla} with the past, for \textquotedblleft{}ago\textquotedblright{}.

Both in one breath:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{سافرت} \ar{بالطائرة} \ar{قبل} \ar{سنة،} \ar{وكانت} \ar{أفضل} \ar{تجربة}.} — \emph{sāfartu bi-ṭ-ṭāʾira qabla sana, wa-kānat afḍala tajriba} — I travelled by plane a year ago, and it was the best experience.
\end{quote}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The plane is faster than the train\textquotedblright{} — \emph{aṭ-ṭāʾira asraʿ min al-qiṭār}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}This pencil case is smaller\textquotedblright{} — \emph{hādhihi al-miqlama aṣghar}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have been waiting for the information since the morning\textquotedblright{} — \emph{antaẓiru al-maʿlūmāt mundhu aṣ-ṣabāḥ}
  \item something you did a year ago, and how long you have done something else
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}Better than\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Afḍal min.}}) \textquotedblleft{}The best experience\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Afḍal tajriba.}}) \textquotedblleft{}For two years\textquotedblright{}, with a present? (\emph{\textbf{Mundhu sanatayn.}}) \textquotedblleft{}A year ago\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Qabla sana.}})
\end{tcolorbox}
